claim: A page type sitting in a folder named its own plural has its pages composed one folder too deep, under a folder named for the type, which no folder shape admits. `namedForTheType` reads the page type's slug and never its `pluralSlug`, so for `story-chapter-read`, whose plural is `chapters` and whose page sits in a folder named `chapters`, `pagesUnder` answers `story/world/stories/read/chapters/story-chapter-read` rather than the folder the type is already in. The Royal Road sync has written three chapter pages there since 2026-09-19 and writes another on every run. folder-matches-a-shape refuses both that folder and the one above it every audit, and it states as a decision that a folder named a plural the page's own type gathers its pages under is right as well. So the shape admits `chapters` for those pages and the composer does not, and the two disagree about one folder.

evidence:
Read on 2026-09-20 out of the checkout.

The composer. `pagesUnder` in page/service/modules/page-composing/page-composing.module.code.ts takes the folder the page type sits in together with the type's slug, and answers that folder with either `pages` or the type's slug appended, choosing between them by `namedForTheType`. That function answers true where the folder's name is the type's slug, or where the slug ends with a dash and that name, and it reads no other property of the type. `story-chapter-read.page-type.ts` states `pluralSlug: "chapters"` and sits in `story/world/stories/read/chapters`, so both clauses are false over `("chapters", "story-chapter-read")` and the composed folder is `story/world/stories/read/chapters/story-chapter-read`.

What landed there. 497a8f35919 moved the chapter read page type under the story read page type. 478460b4edc, `royal road sync 2 page(s)`, then wrote two pages into the composed folder, and af063bdf86d wrote a third after that.

What refuses. The audit at e92f33e37c4c1b48eaaf25fca332bff7d7a9431a had folder-matches-a-shape refuse `story/world/stories/read/chapters` for matching no folder shape, and `story/world/stories/read/chapters/story-chapter-read` for opening with `story-chapter-read`, what the page above it is named.

Where the two disagree. folder-matches-a-shape.check-code.ts states that a folder named a plural the page's own type gathers its pages under is right as well. The shape therefore admits `chapters` as the folder holding those pages. The composer cannot reach that answer, because nothing in `namedForTheType` reads `pluralSlug`.

Neighbouring ground. page-composing.module.test.ts has failed every audit since 2026-09-19T19:53Z asserting `akasha/story/chapter-read/pages/one/one.story-chapter-read.ts`, where that page type sat before 497a8f35919. That test is stale rather than a second reading of the composer.

What is unmeasured. Nothing here has run the composer over another page type whose folder is named that type's plural, so whether this reaches page types besides story-chapter-read is not known.
